brachial fascia: Deep fascia enclosing the arm; with the intermuscular septa it forms the anterior and posterior compartments.
brachialis muscle: Main flexor of the elbow, running from the lower anterior half of the humerus to the ulnar tuberosity. Musculocutaneous nerve (and partly the radial nerve).
brachioradialis muscle: Runs from the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus to the radial styloid process; flexes the half-pronated forearm. Although supplied by the radial nerve, it is a flexor.
bucinator: Muscle forming the wall of the cheek; keeps food between the teeth during chewing and tenses the cheeks when blowing. The parotid duct pierces it. Nerve: facial nerve (buccal branch).
bursa of piriformis muscle: Bursa between the piriformis tendon and the greater trochanter.
calcaneal sulcus: Groove on the upper surface of the calcaneus; with the groove on the talus it forms the sinus tarsi.
calcaneal tendon: Common tendon of gastrocnemius and soleus; the thickest and strongest tendon in the body, it inserts into the calcaneal tuberosity. Rupture is assessed with the Thompson test; it carries the S1 reflex.
calcaneal tubercle: Prominence on the lower front surface of the calcaneus; the plantar ligaments attach to it.
calcaneal tuberosity: Posterior projection of the heel; the Achilles tendon inserts here and it bears weight during standing.
calcaneocuboid ligament: Lateral limb of the bifurcate ligament; binds the calcaneus to the cuboid.
calcaneofibular ligament: Cord running from the tip of the lateral malleolus to the side of the calcaneus; in severe sprains it tears after the anterior talofibular ligament.
calcaneonavicular ligament: Medial limb of the bifurcate ligament; binds the calcaneus to the navicular.
calcaneus: Largest tarsal bone; it forms the heel, and the Achilles tendon inserts into its tuberosity. The flexor hallucis longus tendon passes beneath the sustentaculum tali.
canal for vertebral artery: Canal formed in some people by a bony bridge roofing the groove for the vertebral artery (ponticulus posticus).
capitate bone: Largest carpal bone; it lies in the middle of the distal row and articulates with the 3rd metacarpal. The axis of movement of the hand passes through it.
capitohamate interosseous ligament: Interosseous ligament between the capitate and the hamate.
capitulum of humerus: Rounded articular surface at the lower lateral end of the humerus; forms the humeroradial joint with the radial head.
carotid sulcus: Groove on the side of the body of the sphenoid; the internal carotid artery runs here within the cavernous sinus.
carpal articular surface: Lower articular surface of the radius; forms the wrist joint with the scaphoid and lunate.
carpal bones: Eight short bones arranged in two rows; they form the wrist between the forearm bones and the metacarpus.
cerebral fossa: Upper fossae in which the occipital lobes rest.
cerebral surface of greater wing: Surface of the greater wing facing the middle cranial fossa; the temporal lobe rests against it.
cervical vertebra: Neck vertebra; its transverse process has a foramen.
chiasmatic sulcus: Groove between the two optic canals; it lies next to the optic chiasm.
clavicle: The only long bone lying horizontally, S-shaped; it acts as a strut between the sternum and scapula. It is one of the most commonly fractured bones, usually at the junction of the middle and lateral thirds.
clavicular facet: Small surface of the acromion that articulates with the clavicle.
clavicular head of pectoralis major musc: Upper fibres from the clavicle to the humerus; raise the arm forwards (flexion). Lateral pectoral nerve.
clavicular notch: Superolateral notch of the manubrium; forms the sternoclavicular joint with the clavicle.
clavicular part of deltoid muscle: Anterior fibres; raise the arm forwards and rotate it medially. Axillary nerve (C5–C6).
clavipectoral fascia: Fascia between the clavicle and pectoralis minor; pierced by the cephalic vein, thoracoacromial artery and lateral pectoral nerve.
coccygeal horn: Processes projecting upwards from the base of the coccyx; they articulate with the sacral cornua.
coccygeus muscle: Pelvic diaphragm muscle from the ischial spine to the edge of the sacrum and coccyx; fused with the sacrospinous ligament.
coccyx: Small bone usually formed by the fusion of four rudimentary vertebrae; it gives attachment to the pelvic floor muscles and the anococcygeal ligament.
collateral interphalangeal ligaments of: Collateral ligaments of interphalangeal joints of foot
Side ligaments of the toe joints.
Collateral ligaments of interphalangeal joints of hand
Side ligaments of the finger joints.
collateral metacarpophalangeal ligaments: Side ligaments that tighten in flexion, which is why the hand is splinted with the MCP joints flexed. Injury of the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb is 'skier's thumb'.
collateral metatarsophalangeal ligaments: Side ligaments of the metatarsophalangeal joints.
colliculus of arytenoid cartilage: Small prominence on the anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; where the vestibular ligament attaches.
common extensor tendon: Common tendon of the superficial muscles of the posterior forearm arising from the lateral epicondyle; its degeneration is tennis elbow.
common flexor tendon: Common tendon of the superficial muscles of the anterior forearm arising from the medial epicondyle; its degeneration is golfer's elbow.
common flexor tendon sheath: Sheath enclosing the superficial and deep finger flexor tendons in the carpal tunnel; it is continuous with the little finger sheath.
common tendinous ring: Fibrous ring around the optic canal and the medial part of the superior orbital fissure from which the four rectus muscles arise; the optic, oculomotor, nasociliary and abducens nerves pass through it.
common tendon sheath of fibularis muscle: Common tendon sheath of fibular muscles
Sheath enclosing the two fibular tendons behind the lateral malleolus.
condylar canal: Canal behind the condyle; an emissary vein passes through it.
condyle of humerus: Lower end of the humerus; includes the trochlea, the capitulum and the fossae.
conoid ligament: Medial, cone-shaped part of the coracoclavicular ligament; attaches to the conoid tubercle of the clavicle.
conoid tubercle: Prominence on the lower surface of the lateral end; the conoid part of the coracoclavicular ligament attaches to it.
coraco-acromial ligament: Forms an arch above the humeral head between the coracoid process and the acromion; in subacromial impingement the rotator cuff is trapped under this arch.
